# Acme

> Acme is an example invoicing API for small businesses. This index covers authentication,
> invoice creation and webhooks.

The API uses JSON over HTTPS. Amounts are integers in the currency’s smallest unit. For
example, 1999 represents 19.99 USD.

## Docs

- [Quickstart](https://example.com/docs/quickstart.md): Create a test API key and send an invoice
- [Authentication](https://example.com/docs/authentication.md): API keys, test and live mode, and key rotation
- [Invoices](https://example.com/docs/invoices.md): Create, send, void and list invoices
- [Webhooks](https://example.com/docs/webhooks.md): Event types, payloads and how to verify signatures
- [Errors](https://example.com/docs/errors.md): Error codes and which ones are safe to retry

## API reference

- [OpenAPI specification](https://example.com/openapi.json): Every endpoint, parameter and response schema
- [Node SDK](https://example.com/docs/sdk/typescript): TypeScript client setup and examples

## Product

- [Pricing](https://example.com/pricing.md): Plans, limits and what counts as an invoice
- [Security](https://example.com/security.md): Data storage, encryption and compliance

## Optional

- [Changelog](https://example.com/changelog.md): API changes by version
- [Blog](https://example.com/blog.md): Guides and product news
